purpose: Recruiter-readable capabilities, inspectable mechanisms, and evidence views for the public Decision Log.

primary.label: Product judgment
primary.description: Makes sound product decisions under uncertainty, including scope, sequencing, trade-offs, and what not to build.

primary.label: Product taste
primary.description: Recognizes and creates useful, coherent, and appropriately simple product experiences.

primary.label: Problem framing
primary.description: Turns an ambiguous or messy situation into a clear problem, boundary, and decision.

primary.label: Customer understanding
primary.description: Understands user or customer needs, behaviour, friction, and context well enough to change a product or decision.

primary.label: Operational understanding
primary.description: Understands real workflows, constraints, edge cases, roles, and failure points where work happens.

primary.label: Product discovery
primary.description: Investigates needs, opportunities, assumptions, and solution options before committing to implementation.

primary.label: Prioritization
primary.description: Chooses what deserves attention first based on impact, uncertainty, effort, risk, dependencies, and strategic value.

primary.label: Requirements translation
primary.description: Translates user and business needs into clear scope, requirements, flows, rules, acceptance criteria, or implementation-ready decisions.

primary.label: Execution
primary.description: Moves from ambiguity and decision into concrete delivered work and iteration.

primary.label: Technical fluency
primary.description: Works credibly across product, business, and engineering while understanding systems, APIs, data, architecture, and constraints.

primary.label: Systems thinking
primary.description: Understands dependencies, feedback loops, second-order effects, and how local changes affect a wider system.

primary.label: Quality judgment
primary.description: Defines what good enough means, identifies critical failure modes, and balances quality, speed, and cost.

primary.label: Stakeholder management
primary.description: Understands competing stakeholder needs, creates alignment, and moves decisions or work forward.

primary.label: Operating model design
primary.description: Designs responsibilities, intake, decision rights, handoffs, support, governance, and reusable ways of working.

primary.label: Change management
primary.description: Handles the human and process impact of introducing new systems, products, or ways of working.

primary.label: Adoption and enablement
primary.description: Helps users or teams adopt a product, capability, or new way of working and reach useful time-to-value.

primary.label: Metrics and KPIs
primary.description: Defines how success should be measured and uses relevant metrics to guide decisions and improvement.

primary.label: Value realization
primary.description: Connects work to observable customer, operational, or business value and checks whether intended value is realized.

primary.label: Commercial judgment
primary.description: Reasons about ROI, cost, incentives, pricing, resource allocation, business constraints, and commercial consequences.

primary.label: Evidence discipline
primary.description: Separates fact, evidence, assumption, inference, and outcome while preserving provenance and claim boundaries.

secondary.label: Research judgment
secondary.description: Determines which questions and evidence matter and when evidence is sufficient.

secondary.label: Research synthesis
secondary.description: Combines fragmented information into a concise understanding or actionable recommendation.

secondary.label: Automation judgment
secondary.description: Decides what to automate, what to keep manual, and what level of autonomy is appropriate.

secondary.label: AI systems fluency
secondary.description: Understands practical AI behaviour, tools, context, retrieval, evaluation, traces, failure modes, and human review.

secondary.label: Solution design
secondary.description: Shapes a workable solution across user needs, constraints, flow, and implementation choices.

secondary.label: Root-cause analysis
secondary.description: Separates symptoms from underlying causes and chooses proportionate corrective action.

secondary.label: Reliability
secondary.description: Designs for predictable behaviour despite failures, retries, changing inputs, or partial execution.

secondary.label: Experimentation
secondary.description: Uses bounded tests and staged learning to reduce uncertainty before scaling.

secondary.label: Governance and risk
secondary.description: Identifies risk and encodes appropriate controls, accountability, and fallback paths.

secondary.label: Privacy and security judgment
secondary.description: Makes proportionate privacy and security choices within product and workflow design.

secondary.label: Continuous improvement
secondary.description: Uses reviewed outcomes, failures, and lessons to improve future work.

secondary.label: Ownership
secondary.description: Keeps a problem moving across ambiguity, decisions, delivery, and follow-through.

secondary.label: Delivery management
secondary.description: Coordinates sequencing, dependencies, handoffs, and progress toward a usable result.

secondary.label: Facilitation
secondary.description: Helps people reach shared understanding and make progress through structured discussion.

secondary.label: Cross-functional alignment
secondary.description: Connects different disciplines around a shared decision, scope, or outcome.

secondary.label: Executive communication
secondary.description: Communicates decision-relevant signal, trade-offs, and uncertainty clearly to senior audiences.

secondary.label: Organizational learning
secondary.description: Turns individual experience into reusable knowledge that improves future work.

secondary.label: Technical judgment
secondary.description: Chooses appropriate technical approaches without overengineering or treating technology as the goal.

mechanisms.label: Canary
mechanisms.description: A bounded first exposure used to learn before broader rollout.

mechanisms.label: Human gate
mechanisms.description: A deliberate human approval or intervention boundary.

mechanisms.label: Quality gate
mechanisms.description: An explicit check or pass/fail boundary before work progresses.

mechanisms.label: Validation
mechanisms.description: A test or review that determines whether an assumption or output is ready to proceed.

mechanisms.label: Context engineering
mechanisms.description: Structured instructions, memory, retrieved information, and tools used to improve AI reliability.

mechanisms.label: Workflow automation
mechanisms.description: Repeatable work implemented with controls, exceptions, and review boundaries.

mechanisms.label: Decision traceability
mechanisms.description: A visible link between evidence, assumptions, decisions, implementation, and outcomes.

mechanisms.label: Traceability
mechanisms.description: Provenance links that make inputs, actions, outputs, and decisions inspectable.

mechanisms.label: Improvement loop
mechanisms.description: Reviewed outputs or lessons feeding the next work cycle.

mechanisms.label: Reusable infrastructure
mechanisms.description: Shared foundations, templates, or rules that reduce repeated work.

mechanisms.label: Governance architecture
mechanisms.description: Responsibilities, permissions, boundaries, and operating rules encoded in system structure.

mechanisms.label: Risk controls
mechanisms.description: Concrete safeguards, limits, approvals, and fallback mechanisms.

mechanisms.label: Least privilege
mechanisms.description: Access limited to the authority required for a task.

mechanisms.label: Feedback loop
mechanisms.description: Signals and lessons used to guide the next decision or iteration.

mechanisms.label: Outcome measurement
mechanisms.description: A defined way to observe whether intended value is being realized.

mechanisms.label: Pricing hypothesis
mechanisms.description: A testable commercial assumption, not evidence of willingness to pay.

mechanisms.label: Memory hygiene
mechanisms.description: Keeping accumulated system knowledge relevant, structured, and current.

mechanisms.label: Design governance
mechanisms.description: Explicit design principles and constraints that preserve coherence.

roleLenses.label: AI Product
roleLenses.description: Product decisions, discovery, translation, technical collaboration, quality, and delivery around AI-enabled products.

roleLenses.label: AI Transformation / Enablement
roleLenses.description: Operational change, adoption, governance, and value realization when teams introduce AI-enabled ways of working.

roleLenses.label: Product Ops / Business Analysis
roleLenses.description: Clear problem boundaries, operational detail, requirements, alignment, systems, and measurable improvement.

roleLenses.label: AI Implementation / Customer Enablement
roleLenses.description: Customer context, solution design, technical fluency, delivery, and adoption during implementation.

outcomeStatuses: Success criteria defined but not measured
